findings.claim: Original editor CRT _malloc path 004232E0->00423300->00423350 rounds a 0x78-byte object request to 0x80 and conditionally tries small-block allocation 00425310 before Windows HeapAlloc; original x86 execution confirmed both successes and fallback under controlled threshold/heap results.
findings.limitations: CRT threshold, SBH allocation return and Win32 HeapAlloc were synthetic; normal Windows editor startup configuration and actual heap metadata have not been recovered.

findings.claim: Original 00423300 retries failed CRT allocation when enabled and original 00426230 new-handler dispatcher observes a nonzero callback return. A controlled failure followed by callback true made two native HeapAlloc requests, whereas callback false made one.
findings.limitations: Application new-handler callback was substituted; test does not establish real runtime new-handler installation or retry limits.

findings.claim: Original 00423300 normalizes a zero-byte malloc request to one byte before 16-byte rounding and rejects request 0xFFFFFFE1 without calling allocation or new-handler services.
findings.limitations: Isolated original CRT function tests on synthetic heap, not editor UI authoring.

findings.claim: Within one Ghidra original-instruction emulator state, original 00409840 constructed an editor object using native _malloc, inserted its native 12-byte list node, then original 00409DC0/00409A60/00422FA0 deleted it and directed node then payload frees; zone list head returned to zero.
findings.limitations: Win32 HeapAlloc/HeapFree, CRT small-block free lookup and UI refresh were substituted; no real Windows heap bookkeeping or full process executed.

findings.claim: When native _malloc supplied a valid initialized 0x78-byte payload but list node HeapAlloc returned null, original 0041C430 returned null and 00409840 stored a null head without calling _free or HeapFree during that constructor path, suggesting an ownership cleanup gap.
findings.limitations: No real heap leak was measured; the synthetic allocation failure is not evidence this occurs in typical editor use, nor that no other owner can reclaim memory.

findings.claim: The original constructor at 0040989A writes directly to the returned _malloc pointer, with no preceding null check on the observed native path. Earlier synthetic failure emulation does not establish precise Windows exception or crash behavior.
findings.limitations: Only the missing guard is native-binary supported; actual Windows fault handling, reachability and user-visible behavior remain untested.
